data.narrative:
Electric Era, a Series A climate and energy company founded by Quincy Lee, has raised $11.5M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, a narrow peer-median analysis is not applicable given insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with sufficient data density—nine total sector peers exist, but none of the filtered subsets yielded three or more datapoints needed for reliable triangulation.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable approach. Using total capital raised ($11.5M, rounded to $12M for analysis) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical Series A-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.0x yields an implied valuation of $23M. This reflects standard risk-adjusted progression between stages absent calibration to narrow-set peers.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $20M (low) to $26M (high), with a median of $23M. This single-method triangulation carries meaningful uncertainty. Key dependencies include the appropriateness of the 2.0x stage multiplier to Electric Era's specific risk profile and capital efficiency, and the absence of verifiable same-stage comparables in the Climate & Energy sector to validate the progression assumption. Any valuation conclusion should be treated as preliminary pending access to expanded peer metrics or updated company-specific performance data.
